text:
maria (docs): PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4823 - adding Erebus-13b model card + catalog entry. PTAL for supported variants, seq limits, and quantized compat. I also dropped an SDK example and an embed-sharding note but not 100% on phrasing.

sam (ml eng): taking a look now. Quick q: does Erebus use grouped-attention or sliding-window? that changes the seq ceiling guidance.

maria (docs): Erebus-13b uses grouped-attn with a sliding window fallback for very long contexts. I added an "experimental longctx" callout and a recommended soft limit of 12k tokens.

jen (devex): tiny nit — the bench link you referenced is 404 (the anchor changed): /bench/erebus13 -> ends up 404 on the site.

maria (docs): ah thanks. updated to https://bench.redwood.ai/erebus-13b-v1 — i pulled the 3k-tokens throughput from Sasha's run, can someone confirm those numbers match our internal bench bucket?

dave (infra): numbers look reasonable from the last run, but add a CPU-quant fallback note. on small hosts we fall back to int8-cpu which affects latency. also add a hint about KV cache warming causing higher first-request latency.

maria (docs): good call. adding CPU fallback sentence and a one-liner about cache warmups.

sam (ml eng): also update the embedding examples — for 13B we recommend shard_size=8192 for embedding sharding (cosine) to avoid OOM during batched encode.

maya (mlops): @maria can you add a runtime compatibility row for runtime v2.3? we need to call out multigpu vs single-gpu behavior and which variants are supported by the v2.3 kernel selection.

maria (docs): added a compatibility matrix row for runtime v2.3 + note about hvd not being supported for the quantized 4-bit variant. I also fixed the broken anchor in model card -> hardware-compat.

ci-bot: GitHub / checks — docs-lint failed for PR #4823: anchor link not found (docs/modelcatalog.md#hw-compat).

maria (docs): pushing a hotfix to adjust the anchor and add a redirect entry in the toc.yaml.

sam (ml eng): one more tiny content ask: can we include the micro-bench numbers for sample-lengths 512/2048/3072 in the card? helps product teams map cost. I can re-run and paste numbers after merge if you prefer.

jen (devex): i can take the wording tweak on "soft limit" vs "hard limit" — suggest we use "recommended max (soft)" and "system-enforced" when appropriate. small language change only.

maria (docs): perfect. I'll update the language and re-push. Will wait for CI to pass before merging. thanks for the quick reviews everyone :tada:

sam (ml eng): approving for content pending CI fix. i'll run the micro-benches post-merge and open a follow-up PR to paste numbers into the benchlink table.

dave (infra): lgtm from infra side — added CPU fallback, kv-cache note, and quant-compat warning.

jen (devex): done with copy edits. left one inline comment about the SDK snippet clarity.

maria (docs): adjusted SDK snippet (streaming + async example) per your comment. final snippet in PR: 
```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
# streaming generate example
for chunk in client.generate("erebus-13b", "Summarize the following...", max_tokens=512, streaming=True):
    print(chunk.text)
```

maya (mlops): thanks — don't forget to add the runtime config example for sharding in the card (small snippet on embedding_shard_size).

maria (docs): added the config snippet and a small migration note for teams upgrading from 2.1 -> 2.3.

ci-bot: GitHub / checks — docs-lint passed on PR #4823.

maria (docs): merging after CI green. will follow up with a short changelog entry and a support note in the internal playbook about the CPU fallback. thanks all! :shipit:
